prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Original landscape 3:2 narrative painted illustration for Nihility modular tabletop RPG rulebooks, specifically the Racial Skill section. A clearly nonhuman adult draconic traveler with copper-red scales, a reptilian muzzle and small backward horns, wearing a plain weathered ochre travel tunic and a practical leather belt, uses a controlled short DRACONIC FIRE BREATH to light a pile of damp kindling in a stone hearth at an open roadside shelter. Flame unmistakably emerges from their open mouth toward the kindling, not their hands, with coherent head position, neck and breathing pose. The traveler bends slightly forward in profile, hands safely down at the sides; feet planted, no wings needed, no weapon or magical staff. One human companion in the background prepares a simple cooking pot and watches from a safe distance. A species-specific innate ability used in an ordinary journey, readable quiet story, not a spellcaster gesture or boss fight. Confident traditional acrylic and gouache painted RPG rulebook art, rich natural earth colors, expressive face, believable reptilian anatomy and coherent grip-free hands, selective tactile brushwork, soft edges fading into warm white paper. Overcast late afternoon natural light, small warm fire is local. Strong clear silhouette and mouth-to-hearth line of action. No giant explosion, flames covering the face, floating magic circle, soul, divine spark, circuits, golden core, cosmic imagery, ornamental armor, purple-gold lighting, glossy CGI, text, logos, lettering or labels. This depicts one example of a Racial Skill; it must not imply all species breathe fire.

edits.prompt: Edit the attached Nihility RPG illustration. Change ONLY the fire and its immediately local lighting. Keep the draconic traveler's face, pose, anatomy, clothing, hands, companion, shelter, kettle, landscape, framing and painterly medium unchanged. The current breath looks like a noisy glowing digital streak. Replace it with a SMALLER, SHORTER, physically readable controlled burst of flame from the mouth onto the nearest kindling, painted with a few deliberate irregular flame shapes. A cohesive warm orange flame body, limited pale yellow at the hottest small center, darker translucent orange tips, clear tapered lapping flame edges following the breath direction. Strong reduction in glow, bloom, bright filaments, sparks, spray, glowing dust, particles and tiny disconnected strokes. No electric-looking ribbon, no sparkling jet, no neon outline. The draconic breath must still visibly originate from the mouth and reach the wood, but it should be modest enough to light a hearth, not a continuous dazzling flamethrower. Reduce the fire already on the wood to a few small natural tongues among the kindling. Preserve the original picture's restrained gouache/acrylic brushwork: selective opaque paint shapes for the flame with some transparent edges, not hyperreal VFX pasted on the painting and not a flat orange sticker. Warm light affects only the nearest snout and wood subtly. No added smoke cloud, objects, text or other scene changes.

edits.prompt: Revise this RPG book illustration to FIX THE FIRE by changing the draconic traveler's pose and distance to the wood. Preserve the same adult copper-red draconic character, plain ochre tunic, human companion, mountain shelter, stone hearth, cooking pot, quiet mood and landscape, and the traditional painted rendering. Change the draconic traveler from standing at a distance to crouching/kneeling beside the hearth and leaning forward so the muzzle is VERY CLOSE to a few small dry twigs at the near edge of the hearth, about a hand's length away. Hands can rest safely on the traveler's own bent knees. The breath is only ONE TINY SHORT ORANGE PUFF of fire directly between the mouth and the twigs, with length no greater than the snout itself. It must NOT connect the mouth to the far center of the fire. Eliminate the entire old long snake-like flame ribbon. Nearly all of the air between the traveler and pot should remain clear. The tiny breath should be painted as a few low-contrast warm translucent orange strokes with irregular fading edges and a small yellow center, local to the mouth and nearest twig. The rest of the kindling is only JUST catching: two or three small separate natural flames, no large blaze. Very little glow, no bright white fire core, no glowing outline, no luminous filaments, sparks, particles, long tendril or twisting orange rope. It should feel like an intimate mundane practical use of an innate species ability rather than a cinematic VFX jet. Use simple confident painterly flame marks matching the rest of the artwork, not glossy CGI. Maintain anatomically coherent crouch, clear planted feet, expressive reptilian face and soft pale paper edges. Keep the companion safely behind the hearth with the pot. No added props, captions, magical symbols or extra characters.
